newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News - May 28.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News - May 28.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

In a State Budget designed to win support from business by cutting some taxes and providing incentives while not introducing any new taxes or increasing taxes and charges, the Queensland Government yesterday delivered a Budget with an emphasis on capital works and job creation which will push the State into overall fiscal deficit of A$127 million. Page 1.

In a prelude to a more detailed draft ruling on the issue to be released in July, Tax Commissioner Michael Carmody issued a statement yesterday announcing that the Tax Office will move to stamp out the increasingly popular "split-loan" products which allow consumers to claim tax deductions for the interest on their home loans. Page 3.

The Australian Securities Commission confirmed yesterday its high-security investigations unit in Melbourne was breached during a weekend break-in - the most serious reported incident in the six-year history of the national company regulator. The incident is being investigated by the Federal Police. Page 3.

Despite calls from backbench and industry representatives not to drop post-2000 protection, the Federal Government will receive this week Productivity Commission recommendations understood to reaffirm that tariffs on motor vehicles should be reduced to five per cent by 2004. Page 3.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Speaking during meetings with Prime Minister John Howard and Foreign Affairs Minister Alexander Downer yesterday, Chinese Vice-Premier Zhu Rhongi, the third highest-ranking Chinese leader, said his Government viewed Australia's strategic alliance with the United Staes as neither a threat nor part of a plan to contain China, decisively burying one the main obstacles in relations with Beijing. Page 1.

In a move which Federal Treasurer Peter Costello said had driven mortgage rates to their lowest level since 1969, the ANZ Bank broke ranks with its major rivals yesterday, lowering its home loan mortgage rate to 6.99 per cent. The move comes after an intense Federal Government campaign to force Australia's major banks to match rates on offer from other lenders. Page 1.

According to Roderick West, the chairman of the Federal Government's review of higher education, which reports to the Government in March, Commonwealth funding cuts have damaged the quality of Australia's universities, with tutorials and many quality courses facing the axe. Page 1.

Yesterday's Queensland Budget, which State Treasurer Joan Sheldon said "delivers for all Queenslanders", produced an underlying deficit of A$99 million, sending the State into the red for the first time in a generation, but delivered record spending with the promise of creating 50,000 new jobs and tax cuts. Page 1.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

In statements which put him in direct conflict with the Howard Government, Governor-General Sir William Deane, a former High Court judge, insisted yesterday that the Race Power - Section 51 (xxvi) of the Constitution could only be used for the welfare of indigenous people. Deans also apologised for the forced removal of Aboriginal children from their parents. Page 1.

In a move which comes amid intense opposition to a decision by Australia's four major bank's not to pass on the full benefits of last Friday's official interest rate cut of 0.5 per cent, the ANZ Bank has broken ranks with its competitors, yesterday cutting its standard variable mortgage rate a further 0.21 percentage points to 6.99 per cent. Page 1.

Labor MPs overwhelmingly backed New South Wales Premier Bob Carr yesterday in his moves to establish a committee of inquiry which will report to the State Government in less than three weeks concerning the prospect of a A$22 billion sell-off off New South Wales' electricity industry. Page 1.

In figures which have been severely criticised by the New South Wales Council of Social Service, it has been revealed the State Government underspent its Budget by A$12.6 million in the areas of Community Services, Urban Affairs and Health, despite demand from the State's homeless and needy reaching unprecedented levels. Page 3.
THE AGE

In a speech yesterday marking the thirtieth anniversary of the referendum to recognise Aborigines in the Constitution, Governor-General Sir William Deane offered a personal apology for the separation of Aboriginal children from their parents. The comments came amid growing anger at Prime Minister John Howard over his refusal to acknowledge the issue on behalf of the nation. Page 1.

Thirty-nine-year-old Victorian Bridgitte Muir yesterday became the first Australian woman to climb the highest peaks on the world's seven continents when she scaled Mount Everest with the eight-member British Team Ascent Everest Expedition, originally led by Malcolm Duff, who died in his sleep at the base camp on April 22. Page 1.

Author Faith Bandler, who in 1967 was the general secretary of the Federal Council for the Advancement of Aborigines and Torres Strait Islanders, said yesterday whereas the impediment to reconciliation 30 years ago was ignorance, today it was hatred. Page 1.

In a move which was not followed by its major competitors - the Commonwealth Bank, the National Australia Bank or Westpac - the ANZ Bank yesterday caved in to pressure to pass on last week's official interest rate cut in full by dropping its standard variable home loan rate to a 28-year low of 6.99 per cent. Page 1.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
